projects.title: PokéQuant
projects.tagline: Opening or buying? A reproducible, risk-adjusted comparison of Pokémon TCG booster opening versus buying single cards on the secondary market.
highlights: Slot-level booster model, Bayesian posteriors on community-measured pull rates and a nested Monte Carlo simulation (200 posterior draws × 20,000 runs).
Under central costs the break-even booster price is 1.03 to 1.42 USD, against a retail price of 4.49 USD.
Buying directly is better on the mean, the median and the 5 % CVaR in 35 of 36 comparisons; hypotheses and decision rules were pre-registered.
projects.imageAlt: The PokéQuant web demo: choose a set, a scenario and a budget, and compare opening with buying.

projects.title: Rewrity
projects.tagline: A bilingual (English and French) writing editor: paste a text, get targeted edits with a reason for each, and accept or reject them one by one.
highlights: Returns edits, never a rewritten text: each edit quotes the original, proposes a replacement and says why.
Shows edits as the model writes them, so you can stop once the first ones arrive and keep what has come in.
Reviews by mouse or keyboard, keeps a searchable history, and works in English and French.

projects.title: ORBIT
projects.tagline: An AI-assisted crypto portfolio platform: language-model agents produce numeric market views, and Black-Litterman turns them into portfolio weights.
highlights: The AI never computes an allocation: the optimiser imports nothing from the agent package, and a test pins that absence.
A deterministic risk guard clips the weights, and every correction is logged with its reason.
On 31 backtested periods the edge over holding Bitcoin is statistically indistinguishable from chance, and the site says so.
projects.imageAlt: The ORBIT home page: AI writes the views, mathematics builds the portfolio.

projects.title: Python job listings scraper
projects.tagline: A small web scraper that collects the 100 job listings of the Fake Python Jobs site and saves them to a CSV file.
highlights: Collects title, company, location and link for each job.
Missing fields become empty strings instead of crashing the script.
